source.title: Deep Learning Is Singular, and That’s Good
source.authors: Susan Wei; Daniel Murfet; Ming-Ming Gong; Hui Li; Jesse Gell-Redman; T. Quella

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally compares approximate Bayesian prediction and MAP generalization error on small synthetic regression networks, using KL error rather than the claim versions’ classification-error settings. It also estimates how the RLCT changes with true-distribution complexity.
record.gate_note: The paper’s introductory references to memorizing random labels and classical generalization measures cite prior work; they are not this study’s results. Its own reported results are the synthetic regression experiments in Sections 5–6 and Appendix A.5.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern synthetic regression, approximate Bayesian prediction versus MAP, and RLCT estimation. None tests V1–V8. Its critique of Hessian-based flatness does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its correlation with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors advocate singular learning theory for understanding neural-network generalization, illustrate improvements over MAP using final-layer Bayesian approximations, and find increasing estimated RLCT with increasing true-distribution complexity. They emphasize that applicability to modern large networks and unrealisable distributions remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic regression experiments compare MAP with approximate Bayesian prediction in final layers and estimate RLCT; they do not use the original claim versions’ interventions or classification benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported synthetic generalization results vary with hidden-layer count in the frozen feature block, activation in the final block, realizability, and batch versus minibatch MAP training.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic regression, final-layer or final-two-layer MCMC prediction generally improves KL generalization error over MAP; Laplace approximations perform poorly (Section 5, Table 1 and Appendix A.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate Bayesian prediction in final layers can improve distributional generalization over MAP in small synthetic networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated RLCT increases with true-distribution complexity while the model width remains fixed at five hidden units (Section 6, Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a fixed small network family, RLCT depends on the complexity of the true distribution relative to the model.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical argument establishes Hessian degeneracy for nontrivial ReLU networks and questions curvature-based flatness arguments; it does not evaluate magnitude-scaled perturbation robustness or generalization-gap rankings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-based Laplace arguments require modification for singular neural-network models.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: Experiments use small synthetic regression networks and simulated distributions, not natural classification datasets. The authors note MCMC may find the singular last-two-layer setting more challenging; nonrealisable minibatch results include poor linear fits and missing MAP curve points due to estimated probabilities near zero.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows for the listed versions: the paper’s own numerical outcomes concern synthetic regression generalization error and RLCT, which none of the versions specify. Prior-work citations and figure-only results without separately described version-relevant outcomes are not catalog rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label generalization in the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large-batch penalties and recipe adaptations on image classification or language workloads.
Dropout's effect on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking training–test gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. No version-relevant rows are missing; the unrelated experimental outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels alongside generalization on natural labels.
Widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond interpolation and measuring test error.
Comparing convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Comparing adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum on image or language benchmarks.
Comparing batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Adding or removing dropout and measuring held-out error.
Testing magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
